question.worked_solution:
We perform the multiplication under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{8a{b}^{3}}\cdot 3\sqrt{9b} & = \\ 2\cdot 3\sqrt{8a{b}^{3}\cdot 9b} & = \\ 6\sqrt{72a{b}^{4}} & = \\ 6\sqrt{36{b}^{4}\cdot 2a} & = \\ 6\sqrt{(6{b}^{2})^{2}\cdot 2a} & = \\ 6\sqrt{(6{b}^{2})^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 6\cdot |6{b}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 6\cdot |6|\cdot |{b}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 6\cdot 6\cdot |{b}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{2a}\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot 6\cdot |{b}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 36\cdot {b}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 36{b}^{2}\sqrt{2a}.\end{aligned}
$$
